posts.title: How I keep T&M change orders from turning into argument invoices
posts.text: How I keep T&M change orders from turning into argument invoices Every GC I know has lost money on a "quick" T&M change that somehow became a fight three weeks later. Not because the work was wrong - because nobody could show what was approved, when, and at what rate. Here is the simple log I keep on every job that has any T&M. Works in any spreadsheet. posts.title: What are you running for quote follow-ups and missed calls?
posts.text: hey folks, curious what the room is running these days. im using tradestash for job tracking right now and no complaints there, keeps my crm, quotes, invoices and schedule in one spot which is a big step up from the sticky-note-on-the-dash setup i had before. where im still losing money is two spots it doesnt really cover: follow ups and dealing with missed calls when im on a job. miss two or three a day at times easy and i figure half of those just go call the next guy on the list. what... What are you running for quote follow-ups and missed calls?

posts.title: What do you do when an estimate goes unanswered?
posts.text: Genuine question — I've been talking to a lot of shops lately. You send the quote, hear nothing back. Do you follow up? How many times, and how — call, text, email? Or just move on to the next job? Trying to understand what actually works vs. what everyone means to do but doesn't. What's your process?

posts.title: How do you handle price changes on a job once you're into it?
posts.text: Curious how other guys handle this. I'll quote a job based on what I can see, then get into a wall or under a floor and find rot, bad wiring, whatever — something there was no way to know about walking through it. Now I've got to have the "this is going to cost more" conversation, and even when I'm straight with people about why, some of them hear it as "the guy padded the price after he had me locked in." Had one a while back where the homeowner got a few other quotes after mine changed... How do you handle price changes on a job once you're into it?
